ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure shows a series RC circuit. The upper branch first passes through resistor R, then is connected to the capacitor C on the right side; the current \(\dot I\) flows to the right in the upper wire, and continues through the series path of the resistor and capacitor. The resistor is labeled \(\dot U_R\), and the capacitor is labeled \(\dot U_C\), with its voltage reference direction downward along the capacitor branch. Reasoning: In a series circuit, the same current \(\dot I\) flows through the resistor and capacitor. For a capacitor in sinusoidal steady-state phasor form, there is \(\dot I = j\omega C\dot U_C\). Therefore, when calculating the current using the capacitor voltage, one should multiply by the capacitor admittance \(j\omega C\), rather than divide by \(j\omega C\). So \(\frac{\dot U_C}{j\omega C}\) is an incorrect current calculation formula.

method.method_draft: First describe the image: note that the labeled \(\dot U_C\) is across capacitor \(C\), and the current \(\dot I\) is the series current through that capacitor.
